title.narrative: Output 1.4. Increased capacity of Member States to improve social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
Establishing a basic trade union is a prerequisite for enabling collective bargaining within Ethiopia's labour law framework. In light of this, the Textile Federation (IFTLGWTU) with the support of ONEILO Siraye Programme has successfully organized 18 new basic trade unions across 18 factories, encompassing a total membership of 15,297 individuals (including 11,491 females) strengthening the framework for collective bargaining at the enterprise level. These newly formed unions have undergone capacity-building training sessions focusing on leadership, labour law, and the principles of collective bargaining.
The ILO supported the dialogue between IFTLGWTU and the Investors’ Association to strengthen bipartite mechanisms of grievance handling in the Industrial Parks with the active involvement of Government. As a result workers’ call centres have been established in Hawassa and Bole Lemi Industrial Parks to offer workers an alternative means to report grievances and receive comprehensive support towards their resolution. Additionally, the centres offer information to workers regarding their rights and responsibilities.
With Hawassa University, the ILO established two new and strengthened an existing legal aid centre, all of which provide free legal aid to workers and vulnerable community members. Since they began, the centres have handled 512 cases, 45% related to labour issues. The estimated value of the services provided by the centres is at least USD 80,000. Private attorney firms typically charge between 250 and 350 USD for a single case, unaffordable for most workers. The non-monetary value and impact of this service extend beyond measure.
ILO extended financial and technical support to the Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association (EWLA), to offer free legal aid services for workers, the majority female. Advancing Decent Work and Inclusive Industrialization (ONEILO Siraye) Programme provided training and developed awareness training materials and financial support to CETU, the Textile Federation, Hawassa University, and the Ethiopian Women Lawyers Association.
Two rounds of industry seminars were rolled out on the topic of workplace cooperation and grievance handling to share ideas on some of the concrete challenges factories are facing regarding the collective bargaining process and workplace cooperation mechanisms.
The programme conducted workplace cooperation training in one factory targeting trade unions and management representatives to equip participants with the tools needed to improve business performance through better workplace cooperation practices.
Workplace communication training targeting workers at the operator level was rolled out virtually and in person, reaching 262 workers (233 female). The aim was to create awareness of workplace communication.

description.narrative: The ILO’s Results Framework is always part of the Programme and Budget (P&B) document for the relevant biennium. Please refer to the Annex “Results Framework” of the relevant P&B Document

The ILO’s biennial Programme Implementation Report is an instrument of accountability. It describes the performance of the Organization against the commitments made in the Programme and Budget documents for the corresponding biennial period.
